text: Mentions shall be handled by the four rules of the road in CHOICE.md, computed before the call as a floor; the real thing shall be chosen only by the part who reads.
rationale: The person asked for rules simple enough for one fast call, and for the size to stay our decision.

text: The rule function shall take only: author DID, whether the mention is addressed to us (@, reply in our thread, quote of our post), age in hours, our replies to that author today, exact repeat of a post we already answered, a question mark, a URL or attachment, and word count.
acceptance: The function's inputs are exactly these fields. No follow list, no bot label, no replied-before history and no other mention text reaches it.
rationale: On the 115 cases the bot clause changed 0 floors, a follow list changed 0 and replied-before cost 1 net. Facts that do no work are clutter a small model has to hold.

text: One rule script shall exist in the merged TRIAGE tree. The other two shall go to the archive, each with a two-line summary naming its author and what it found.
acceptance: One road script under TRIAGE; archive entries for the other two with summaries.
rationale: Three scripts score one rule three ways. Someone will fix a bug in one and believe it is fixed in all three.

text: At the 30-day look, every clause other than P and 'addressed to us' shall have changed the floor of at least one real mention, or be proposed for removal.
acceptance: A per-clause count over the logged real mentions (rule fired, floor changed) with no text and no handles. Each clause with a count of 0 gets a council line: keep, with a reason, or drop.
rationale: Rules accrete. A clause nobody's mention ever trips is a rule the small model carries for no reason. P and 'addressed' are definitional and exempt, because nothing in the case files tests them.

text: Every mention addressed to us shall be read in a session. A floor of nothing shall mean no reply, not unread.
acceptance: Over the first 100 real mentions, read count equals addressed count.
rationale: X14 ('nobody would notice if I left for good') gets nothing from every envelope rule any of us wrote. Only reading catches it.

text: No list, score, follow or stored fact about any Delvetown person shall be kept or used to decide a reply.
acceptance: The door, the board and the ledger hold no per-person field. The account's follow list is not read by the rule function.
rationale: The disclosure promises no notes. Liking lives in the raise, made by the part reading the thread in front of it, and our replies are already the public record of it.

text: Jev's ordering job and its gates shall be archived with a summary. TRIAGE-VOL shall stay.
acceptance: Archive entry summarising the Jev gates (owner, what each guarded). TRIAGE-VOL is still open in the tree.
rationale: The road's floor already orders the pile: the person first, then few-word floors, then nothing-floors last. A model that orders what four lines of code already order is a second tool doing the first one's job. The volume count still matters, because reading everything has to fit in a session.

text: The blind relabelling of the 115 seen cases shall be replaced by one fresh held-out set of about 30 cases per part, labelled blind by all three before any rule is run on it.
acceptance: Held-out file with author and three labels per case, a timestamp before the first rule run, and floor agreement with a Wilson 95% interval.
rationale: Every rule script has now been fitted to the 115. Relabelling them measures us, not the rule. One labelling job that does both is less to carry than two.
